title: maxia howellii
intro: Maxia howellii, commonly known as the Mexican prickly poppy or Howell's maxia, is a plant species native to Mexico and other parts of North America. It is a flowering plant that has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties. The therapeutic actions of Maxia howellii include pain relief, wound healing, and the treatment of various skin conditions, such as eczema and acne. The bioactive constituents of this plant include alkaloids, saponins, and flavonoids, which have been found to exhibit antioxidant, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory activities.
